chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Atlantic session in 1959 and the Floyd Dixon album in 1960
summary: Atlantic was the only session Smith was paid for; a 1960 Fort Worth album with Floyd Dixon went unpaid, and they discuss his band including drummer Robert Cobbs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: That's interesting. And did you not get paid at all, or did you just get a fee for the recording and then you didn't royalties?
I didn't get nothin'. Not a dime. Didn't get a thing. The only one I got paid for recording was the Atlantic Recording Company.
The one in '59.
The one that ...(?)..> That's the one I got paid.
That's really interesting. So there are records of you around if only they could be found.
Yeah. And I made one with old Floyd Dixon, went over there and paid all the transportation and everything, and took my boys over there, and he...
Where was this?
Fort Worth. That's where we recorded it. We made that Atlantic record in Fort Worth, on West 70... They've got a good studio over there. And this here guy who was supposed to be
Buster Smith - 131
behind this record we did with Floyd Dixon lived in Tennessee. I believe it was Nashville, Tennessee.
Was he a White guy or a Black guy?

A White guy. No, he wasn't in Tennessee. Mississippi. Yeah, down in Mississippi. Yeah, Jackson, Mississippi is where he was. He had Floyd there to make this big album, a big album just like that one you seen here. And a whole lot of numbers were on that that I made up. Floyd and I had a ...(?).... sitting up there. For nine days we sits here and made that program up. I got the band rehearsing. We went over there and rehearsed, I mean we recorded, til the middle of the morning. And I never did get a nickel. Didn't get a dime.
Do you know if the record ever came out?

Yeah, the record's out. Yeah, it came out, but I never did get ...(?)... They came out on the 45's. Most of them are out in 45. And Floyd got some money from the man, and then Bernie(?) McCall left here and went on down to Corpus Christi. They tell me he's down there in jail now, and done something down there.
He's in jail.
Yeah.
Can you remember what year this was?
That was after I made that record in '59. It was in '60.
Buster Smith - 132
One year later.
Yeah. A year later.
It wasn't the same band that recorded on Atlantic.
Yeah. Same band.
You didn't think of changing the band.
Oh, no.
Because the band could have been improved..
Yeah, well...
There are three strong guys on that band -- Herman Flowers, you and Leroy Cooper. The others could be a bit...

Yeah. See, we didn't have very good musicians living around here, and I kept the same boys all the time. I didn't care if they wasn't no outstanding musicians. I'd write according to their ability. In fact, for the whole band, because I didn't put nothin' too stiff where they couldn't play. Better for them to play something...
I think the soloists, the front line is all right. The only thing that worries me a bit is the drummer.
Yeah, the drummer...
He's a big heavy. The music doesn't swing (?)
Yeah, that's old Cobbs. Robert Cobbs on drums. He lives down here in Waxahachie(?).
He's still around.
Yeah. He's working at the funeral home down
